weeks.summary: You're both brand new at this. This week is about feeding, sleeping and healing — nothing more is required of anyone.

happening.b: Most newborns feed 8–12 times per 24 hours. A tiny stomach means small, frequent meals — day and night. Weight commonly dips a few percent after birth and starts climbing back within days.
Expect 14–17 hours of sleep in short stretches of 1–3 hours, with no day/night pattern yet. That's typical for week one.
The umbilical cord stump is drying out — keep it clean and dry until it falls off on its own (usually 1–3 weeks). Skin may peel or look blotchy; both are commonly seen.

todo: Feed on hunger cues (rooting, hand-to-mouth) rather than the clock
Always place baby on the back to sleep, on a firm flat surface, no loose bedding
Sleep when the baby sleeps — this week that's a survival rule, not a cliché
weeks.watching: Fewer than 6 wet diapers a day after day 5, a rectal temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, unusual sleepiness or refusal to feed — call your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Adaptation week: most of the newborn transition states peak and start to fade by the end of this week.

happening.b: A yellow tint to skin and eyes is very commonly seen — it usually peaks around days 3–5 and fades by the end of week 2. Frequent feeding helps it pass.
You may briefly see reddish-orange dust in the diaper (urate crystals) in the first days; it typically disappears as feeding volume grows.
Mild breast swelling or a little discharge can appear in both boys and girls as maternal hormones leave the body. It's painless, symmetric and temporary.

todo: Keep gentle hygiene: warm water is enough for most of the body
Avoid overheating — light layers, room around 68–72°F
Note feeds and diapers; the counts answer half of your worries
weeks.watching: Yellow tint spreading below the knees, deepening after day 5, or paired with poor feeding or unusual sleepiness — call your pediatrician the same day.

weeks.summary: A hungry, clingy stretch is common around now — many babies hit their first big growth spurt.

happening.b: Feeding every 30–60 minutes for a few hours, often in the evening, is commonly seen and usually signals a growth spurt — not low milk supply.
Awake windows stretch a little. Baby focuses best 8–12 inches away — exactly the distance to your face during feeds.
By now most babies are back to birth weight and gaining roughly 5–7 oz a week.

todo: Follow the appetite — supply adjusts to demand
Use short awake windows for face-to-face time and gentle tummy time
Hand off one stretch a day to a partner if you can
weeks.watching: No return to birth weight by the two-week checkup, or consistently fewer than 6 wet diapers a day — bring it up with your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Crying starts climbing toward its normal peak. It's a phase with a shape — it rises, peaks, and falls.

happening.b: Total daily crying commonly increases from around week 2, peaks near month 2, and eases by months 3–4. Some of it has no findable reason — that's part of normal development.
The 'witching hour' — a fussy stretch in the late afternoon or evening — is one of the most commonly reported patterns at this age.
During tummy time many babies briefly lift the head and turn it side to side.

todo: Build a soothing rotation: hold, rock, feed, white noise, fresh air
It's okay to put baby down safely and step away for a few minutes if you feel overwhelmed — that protects both of you
Never shake a baby — hand them to someone or put them down safely instead
weeks.watching: A cry that sounds unlike your baby (high-pitched, weak) plus fever, vomiting or refusal to feed — call your pediatrician now.

weeks.summary: For many babies this is the loudest stretch. You're not doing anything wrong — the curve just hasn't turned yet.

happening.b: Daily crying is close to its natural maximum for many babies around weeks 5–8. Soothing helps in the moment; time is what actually ends it.
Baby follows your face in a small arc and studies high-contrast patterns.
Little throaty noises and early cooing may show up in calm moments.

todo: Trade shifts with a partner during the evening peak
Take crying breaks in another room when you need them — a safely placed crying baby is okay for a few minutes
Track sleep to spot the day's calmest window and protect it for yourself
weeks.watching: Crying paired with fever 100.4°F+, vomiting (not spit-up), fewer wet diapers, or a bulging soft spot — call your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: The payoff week: social smiles often arrive right when parents need them most.

happening.b: By around 2 months most babies smile in response to you — not just gas. If it hasn't happened yet, the window is still wide open.
Baby quiets or turns toward a familiar voice more reliably now.
A growth spurt around week 6 is commonly seen — expect a hungrier couple of days.

todo: Talk and sing face-to-face during awake windows — conversation is development
Keep tummy time daily, a few minutes at a time
Book the 2-month checkup if you haven't yet
weeks.watching: By 2 months: no response to loud sounds, or not watching things as they move — mention it at the checkup.

weeks.summary: Awake time gets genuinely interactive: more looking, more cooing, more of baby showing up as a person.

happening.b: Vowel sounds ('ooo', 'aah') appear and baby may 'answer' when you pause — the first turn-taking.
Self-soothing via hands and fists is commonly seen and completely fine.
For many babies the crying curve begins its slow descent around now.

todo: Narrate your day out loud — it's language input, not silliness
Offer a high-contrast toy to track side to side
Start a simple, repeatable wind-down before night sleep
weeks.watching: Baby doesn't calm at all when held and fed, most days — worth a conversation with your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: The 2-month visit: measurements, milestones and the first big round of vaccines.

happening.b: Around now most babies smile at people, calm when spoken to or picked up, watch you as you move, and hold the head up in tummy time.
Expect brief crying, extra sleepiness or mild fussiness for a day or so afterward — commonly seen. Your pediatrician will tell you what's expected and what's not.
Jerky newborn movements are giving way to smoother arm and leg motion.

todo: Write your questions down before the visit — the checklist in Ask can help
Plan a quiet day after vaccines
Comfort works: feeding and holding right after shots measurably helps
weeks.watching: After vaccines: fever above 104°F, crying inconsolably for 3+ hours, or anything that worries you — call your pediatrician; that's what they're for.

weeks.summary: More sounds, more smiles, and the first hints of a daily rhythm.

happening.b: Squeals, gurgles and longer coo strings — baby is playing with the voice.
Feeds and naps start clumping at similar times. It's a sketch, not a schedule — expect it to wobble.
Head comes up higher and holds longer; some babies start pushing up on forearms.

todo: Follow the sketch: aim naps at the sleepy cues, not the clock
Answer baby's sounds like a conversation — pause, reply, pause
Move tummy time to a firm floor mat for better practice
weeks.watching: No cooing or vocal sounds at all, and no social smiling by now — mention it to your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Night sleep often consolidates a little — some babies gift you a 4–6 hour stretch.

happening.b: Many babies begin sleeping one longer block at night. Many others don't yet — both are commonly seen at this age.
Staring at hands, bringing them together, gnawing on fists — baby is discovering the body.
Salivary glands wake up around now. Drooling alone isn't teething yet.

todo: Keep night interactions boring: dim light, quiet voice, no play
Protect your own sleep during the long stretch — go to bed early once
Offer safe objects to grasp and mouth
weeks.watching: Baby who slept longer stretches suddenly waking hourly for many nights plus feeding poorly — worth a pediatrician chat.

weeks.summary: Swiping, batting, grabbing at things — movement gets intentional.

happening.b: Baby bats at dangling toys and may briefly hold what lands in the hand.
Held upright, the head is steadier with less wobble.
Familiar faces get faster smiles; new faces get long study.

todo: Hang a toy within batting range during floor play
Practice supported sitting on your lap for short spells
Keep narrating — receptive language is building fast
weeks.watching: Very stiff or very floppy body most of the time — bring it up with your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: The newborn fog is lifting: more laughter, longer awake windows, real personality.

happening.b: For most babies daily crying is clearly less than a month ago.
Chest comes off the floor on forearms; some babies attempt tiny pre-rolls — never leave baby on raised surfaces.
First laughs commonly land around 3–4 months; the warm-up sounds are here.

todo: Childproof changing routines: one hand on baby, always
Stretch awake windows gently — overtired babies sleep worse, not better
Celebrate: you got through the hardest quarter
weeks.watching: Not holding the head up in tummy time, or not smiling at people by 3 months — discuss at your next visit.

weeks.summary: Three months: the 'fourth trimester' ends. Rhythms firm up and the world gets interesting.

happening.b: Play sessions stretch; baby tracks across the whole room and turns toward sounds.
Somewhere in the next month sleep architecture matures — night waking can temporarily increase before it improves. Forewarned is forearmed.
Toys are held, shaken and brought straight to the mouth.

todo: Refresh the sleep basics before the 4-month shift: dark room, consistent wind-down
Rotate a few simple toys — novelty beats quantity
Take the 3-month photo you'll want later
weeks.watching: Loss of any skill baby previously had is always worth a call to your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: The fourth trimester is behind you. A hungrier stretch is commonly seen around now — and awake time turns genuinely social.

happening.b: A growth spurt around three months is commonly seen: more feeds, more clinginess for a few days, then it settles.
Staring at hands, clasping them, pulling everything to the mouth — this is how the brain maps the body.
Salivary glands are fully awake. Drool alone isn't teething yet — teeth commonly arrive later.

todo: Feed on demand through the spurt — supply follows
Rotate two or three simple graspable toys
Keep the wind-down routine steady even on hungry days
weeks.watching: Feeding refusal (not just fussiness), fewer wet diapers, or fever 100.4°F+ — call your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Squeals, chuckles and maybe a full laugh — sound play is the theme of the week.

happening.b: First real laughs commonly land around 3–4 months. Tickles, silly sounds and peek-a-boo warm-ups are the usual triggers.
In tummy time the chest comes up on forearms; some babies start pivoting in a circle.
Side-tipping and half-rolls appear — from now on, never leave baby on any raised surface, even for a second.

todo: Move diaper changes to low, safe surfaces now — before the first surprise roll
Give floor time daily; the floor is the gym
Answer every sound — pause, reply, pause
weeks.watching: No smiling at people, or baby doesn't calm with comfort most of the time — mention to your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Welcome to the famous 4-month sleep shift: sleep architecture matures, and nights commonly get bumpier before they get better.

happening.b: Baby's sleep is reorganizing into adult-like cycles with light phases every 45–60 minutes. More brief night wakings are commonly seen — it's development, not a step back.
How baby falls asleep at bedtime is what they look for at 2 AM. Practicing drowsy-but-awake at bedtime commonly pays off at night.
Thirty-to-forty-minute 'one-cycle' naps are typical during the shift.

todo: Protect the basics: dark room, consistent wind-down, same sleep space
Pick one bedtime approach and hold it for two weeks before judging
Split the night into shifts with your partner — this stretch is a marathon
weeks.watching: Night waking plus fever, ear pulling with distress, or feeding falling off — that's a pediatrician call, not a sleep phase.

weeks.summary: Checkup and second vaccine round — plan a soft week around it while the sleep shift is still doing its thing.

happening.b: Around now most babies hold the head steady unsupported, push up to elbows in tummy time, laugh or squeal, and bring hands to the mouth constantly.
Same playbook as two months: brief crying, extra sleepiness or mild fussiness for a day is commonly seen. Feeding and holding right after the shots genuinely helps.
Many babies land the first full roll around now — usually tummy to back first, often to their own surprise.

todo: Bring your question list — the doctor visit sets in Ask can help
Stop swaddling completely once rolling starts, if you haven't already
Plan nothing ambitious for vaccine day
weeks.watching: After vaccines: fever above 104°F, inconsolable crying 3+ hours, or anything that worries you — call your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: New skill, restless nights: babies commonly practice rolling in their sleep exactly when you'd prefer they didn't.

happening.b: Brains rehearse new motor skills during sleep. A baby who flips over and complains is commonly seen for a few weeks around each new skill.

happening.t: Back to sleep, always start there
happening.b: Keep placing baby on the back for every sleep. Once baby rolls both ways on their own, they may stay where they roll — but the sleep space must be completely bare.
Swipes become grabs; whatever is within reach is now baby's property and goes straight to the mouth.

todo: Audit the sleep space again: nothing loose, nothing within pull distance
Move small objects out of arm's reach during floor time
Keep bedtime boring and identical every night
weeks.watching: Baby stuck face-down and unable to turn the head to breathe comfortably — reposition and mention it at your next visit; hard-to-rouse or breathing that looks laboured is urgent care.

weeks.summary: For many families the sleep shift eases; awake windows stretch and the day finds a 3-nap shape.

happening.b: Roughly three naps with longer awake windows in between is the commonly seen shape now. It's still a sketch — growth days will bend it.
Baby watches your mouth, 'answers' in coos and squeals, and repeats sound games. Narrate your day — it all counts.
Texture testing by mouth is the main science program at this age. Keep chokeable objects (anything that fits through a toilet-paper tube) away.

todo: Aim naps at sleepy cues within the loose 3-nap frame
Offer toys with different textures — safe, big, washable
Take the break when it comes: calm weeks are for refilling your own tank
weeks.watching: Loss of a skill baby already had is always worth a pediatrician call.

weeks.summary: Drool by the litre, everything in the mouth, cranky evenings — the pre-teeth season commonly opens around now, even if the first tooth is months away.

happening.b: Extra drool, gum rubbing, chewing on everything, mild fussiness. What it commonly does NOT cause: high fever, diarrhea or rash — those mean something else and deserve a pediatrician call.
Anywhere from ~4 to 12+ months is commonly seen; bottom front teeth usually lead.
A refrigerated (not frozen) teether or a clean cool washcloth to chew is the safe go-to. Skip teething gels and amber necklaces — pediatric guidance advises against both.

todo: Stock two or three solid one-piece teethers
Wipe the chin often — drool rash prevention is easier than treatment
Keep evening expectations low on cranky days
weeks.watching: Fever 100.4°F+, refusal to feed, or diarrhea — don't file it under teething; call your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Back-to-tummy commonly joins the repertoire — and the floor becomes a training field.

happening.b: Once both directions click, rolling becomes transport. Supervised floor freedom is the best gift you can give this skill.
Propped on your lap or between your legs, baby holds the tripod pose for moments at a time.
Passing a toy hand to hand and holding two things at once are commonly seen wins around this stretch.

todo: Clear a floor zone: blanket, three toys, zero small objects
Practice supported sitting a few minutes a day
Lower the crib mattress if it's still on the newborn height
weeks.watching: Body consistently stiff or floppy, or strong preference for using only one side — bring it up with your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: 'Ba', 'da', 'ma' — consonants enter the chat, and it starts sounding like speech rehearsal.

happening.b: Strings like 'ba-ba' commonly appear around 5–6 months. It's sound practice, not naming yet — but respond as if it's conversation, because that's how it becomes one.
Shake makes noise, drop makes parent pick up — baby is running experiments on the world (and on you).
Many babies now do a solid long stretch at night; many don't yet. Both are commonly seen — your logged trend matters more than any single night.

todo: Play turn-taking sound games — copy baby's syllable, wait, repeat
Introduce a simple shaker or crinkle toy
Compare this week's sleep chart to last month's — progress hides in trends
weeks.watching: No babbling sounds at all and no turning toward voices — mention to your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Stronger back, better balance: sitting with less and less support is the project of the week.

happening.b: Baby props on hands in front, holds a few seconds, topples sideways — every fall is a data point for the balance system. Cushion the landing zone and let the reps happen.
Eyes now track fast movement and study small details; mirrors become fascinating.
Distracted eating is commonly seen — the world is more interesting than the meal. Quieter, dimmer feeds help.

todo: Build a cushion ring for sitting practice
Add a baby-safe mirror to floor time
Feed in a low-stimulation corner if feeds got wiggly
weeks.watching: Fewer wet diapers or clear feeding refusal beyond distraction — call your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Half a year is close — time to read the readiness signs for first foods and let baby study your dinner like a textbook.

happening.b: Commonly used markers: sits with minimal support, steady head, reaches for your food, and the tongue no longer pushes everything straight out. Most babies line these up around six months — your pediatrician confirms the go.
Whatever the excitement, breast milk or formula remains the main nutrition for months ahead; first foods are practice, not replacement.
A pre-six-month growth spurt is commonly seen — hungrier days, extra feeds, then back to baseline.

todo: Discuss the solids plan at the 6-month visit — including how your family wants to handle common allergens
Get the gear minimal: high chair with straps, soft spoons, bibs you don't love
Let baby watch family meals — appetite is social
weeks.watching: Poor weight gain or feeding refusal beyond distraction — bring to your pediatrician before starting solids.

weeks.summary: Strength everywhere: sitting firms up, feet are discovered (and tasted), and the pre-solids appetite runs hot.

happening.b: Longer solo sits with hands free for toys are commonly seen around the half-year mark.
Grabbing feet and pulling them to the mouth is peak flexibility — enjoy the acrobatics phase.
Two-to-three naps and a long night block is the commonly seen shape; if nights wobble, it's usually skill practice or the upcoming teeth.

todo: Book the 6-month checkup
Baby-proof one level down: floor-level cables, plants, small objects
Photo idea: the foot-in-mouth pose does not last
weeks.watching: Loss of any acquired skill — always a pediatrician call.

weeks.summary: Happy half-birthday: the 6-month checkup, another vaccine round, and — with your pediatrician's go — the first spoon.

happening.b: Around now most babies know familiar people, love mirror games, take turns making sounds, roll both ways and sit with support or briefly alone.

Start with single-ingredient purees or soft mashed foods once a day; iron-rich options are commonly recommended first. One new food at a time, a few days apart, makes reactions easy to spot. Gagging looks scary and is commonly seen; it's the learning reflex — silent choking is the emergency.
Same expectations as before: a sleepy, clingy day is commonly seen. Comfort works.

todo: Do the first solids attempt on a calm morning, not vaccine day
Learn infant choking first aid this week — 10 minutes that buy peace of mind
Keep milk feeds unchanged for now
weeks.watching: Feeding reactions with hives, facial swelling, vomiting — call your pediatrician; struggling to breathe after food — 911.

weeks.summary: The lab is open: textures, tastes and spectacular faces. Everything about early solids is experiments — including the mess.

happening.b: Grimaces at new foods are commonly seen and don't mean 'never' — it can take many exposures for a food to land. Keep offering without pressure.
Iron-rich foods (iron-fortified cereal, pureed meats, beans) are commonly emphasized at this stage because newborn iron stores run down around six months.
Small sips of water with meals commonly start now; milk remains the main drink.

todo: Offer one meal a day, follow baby's lead on amount
Re-offer rejected foods later — persistence without pressure
A washable floor mat under the high chair saves sanity
weeks.watching: Blood in stool, hives, or repeated vomiting after a new food — call your pediatrician the same day.

weeks.summary: Object permanence is loading: dropped toys get searched for, hidden things exist now — and so does missing you.

happening.b: Baby now knows the hidden thing still exists — that's why peek-a-boo suddenly produces full-body laughter.
Wariness with new faces and extra clinginess with you are commonly seen from around now. It's attachment working, not regression in social skills.
Throwing things to watch you retrieve them is gravity research with a social bonus. Annoying and completely on schedule.

todo: Play hiding games — a toy under a cloth is the perfect level
Give new people a slow warm-up next to you
Attach toys to the high chair with short clips if the drop game wears you down
weeks.watching: No response to own name and no babbling by now — mention at your pediatric visit.

weeks.summary: Independent sitting commonly locks in around now — hands free, posture proud, world at a new angle.

happening.b: Solid solo sitting frees both hands for serious toy work: banging two things together is the hit single of the month.
Pivoting on the belly, pushing backwards, rocking on hands and knees — the launch sequence is loading in whatever order your baby prefers. Some skip crawling entirely; commonly seen and fine.
Many babies consolidate toward two longer naps around this stretch; the transition weeks are commonly bumpy.

todo: Get on the floor at eye level — it's the best play position now
Give push-worthy targets: a toy just out of reach motivates movement
If naps are chaos, hold a loose 2-nap frame for a week before changing course
weeks.watching: Can't sit even with support, or strongly favors one side — bring to your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Rocking, scooting, reverse gear: locomotion is imminent, and the house is about to feel much smaller.

happening.b: Hands-and-knees rocking commonly precedes crawling by a few weeks. Backwards motion often comes first — the engine works, the steering is learning.
Before movement starts, do the crawl-test yourself: outlets, cords, stair gates, cabinet locks, anchored furniture, small objects at floor level.
Long babble runs — 'bababa', 'dadada' — are commonly seen; they're speech scaffolding, not names yet (whatever grandpa claims about 'dada').

todo: Babyproof one room completely as the free-roam zone
Anchor tall furniture and the TV — this is the week
Cheer the effort, not just the result: struggle is the workout
weeks.watching: Persistent stiffness, floppiness, or no interest in moving toward toys — discuss with your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Fingers get smart: raking little objects, passing hand to hand, inspecting everything from every side.

happening.b: Whole-hand raking of small items is commonly seen now; the delicate thumb-finger pincer arrives closer to nine months. Either way, floor-level small-object patrol is now a daily chore.
Turning objects over, switching hands, mouthing then studying again — this is how material science is done at seven months.
Baby wants to grab the spoon and the food. Soft finger-food pieces (melt-in-mouth, no round hard shapes) commonly enter around now if solids are going well.

todo: Do a daily floor sweep for coin-sized objects — the toilet-roll-tube test
Offer two toys at once to work the hand-to-hand pass
Let one spoon be baby's while you use another — shared control, less battle
weeks.watching: Choking-risk foods to skip everywhere: whole grapes, nuts, popcorn, hot dog rounds, hard raw veg.

weeks.summary: Separation awareness commonly peaks into a clingy stretch: leaving the room becomes an event. It's love with an alarm system.

happening.b: Crying when you leave — even to the bathroom — is commonly seen from around now and can flare at bedtime too. It means attachment built correctly; it fades as memory learns that you always come back.
Sneaking away commonly backfires; a quick cheerful 'be right back' plus consistent return builds the trust muscle faster.
Some babies now wake just to check you exist. A calm, boring, brief response is the commonly recommended tone.

todo: Practice mini-separations at home: narrate, leave, return, repeat
Keep bedtime routine extra consistent through the clingy weeks
Hand baby to the sitter awake with a proper goodbye, not mid-sleep
weeks.watching: Distress that never settles with comfort, or a baby who stops engaging with familiar people — pediatrician conversation.

weeks.summary: Rocking turns into lurching, lurching into the first honest crawl for many babies over the coming weeks — in whatever style {name} invents.

happening.b: Classic cross-crawl, army-drag, crab-scoot, bottom-shuffle — all commonly seen, all legitimate transport. Some babies skip crawling entirely and go straight to pulling up; also normal.
New mileage burns fuel: a hungrier stretch with bigger solid-food interest is commonly seen as movement takes off.
Motor leaps commonly rehearse at night — expect a few nights of crib gymnastics.

todo: Open the floor: the proofed free-roam zone earns its keep now
Put one favorite toy just out of reach each floor session
Recheck outlet covers and cord routes at new reach height
weeks.watching: No attempts to move toward objects at all, or one side clearly dragging — mention at your pediatrician visit.

weeks.summary: Hidden things exist now: {name} lifts cups to find toys, hunts dropped spoons and studies how objects relate.

happening.b: Putting things IN and dumping things OUT becomes the main research program — a muffin tin and soft blocks equal a laboratory.
Baby now pulls the cloth off YOUR face and laughs before the reveal — prediction, memory and humor working together.
Long strings with adult-like intonation — it sounds like a foreign language argument, and it's speech rehearsal.

todo: Play hide-the-toy under one of two cups — slow reveal
Narrate object games: in, out, under, gone, found
Rotate toys weekly — familiar plus one new beats a toy mountain
weeks.watching: No babbling at all by now, or no response to own name — bring to the pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Stranger wariness commonly sharpens: the same grandma who got smiles last month may get suspicion first. It's memory, not manners.

happening.b: Baby now firmly knows who's who — and treats unknown faces as pending review. Commonly seen from 8 months and often lasting well into the second year in waves.
Visitors succeed by ignoring baby at first: talk to you, stay at distance, let baby approach. Handing baby over cold commonly backfires.
Expect check-back-and-explore loops: crawl away, look back, return, repeat. You're the charging dock.

todo: Brief visitors on the slow-warm rule before they arrive
Keep hellos and handoffs unhurried — baby sets the pace
Practice short separations at home with cheerful returns
weeks.watching: Total absence of preference for familiar people is worth mentioning at a visit.

weeks.summary: The 9-month checkup approaches: a screening-heavy visit — development questionnaire, growth, feeding review, usually no shots.

happening.b: Around now: solid solo sitting, working toward pulling up, raking grasp refining toward finger-tip pincer, responds to own name, plays interactive games.
Many practices run a standardized development screen at 9 months — your honest everyday observations matter more than a good performance in the office.
Soft, melt-in-mouth pieces baby can self-feed commonly become the star — messy self-feeding IS the skill being built.

todo: Bring your logs and Ask doctor-notes to the visit
List any asymmetries or worries — 9 months is a great catch-early point
Offer two finger-food textures at family meals
weeks.watching: Choking-risk foods stay banned: whole grapes, nuts, popcorn, hot-dog rounds, hard raw veg.

weeks.summary: Furniture becomes gym equipment: pulling to stand commonly starts — along with the famous 8–10-month sleep wobble.

happening.b: Crib rails, couch edges, your legs — everything vertical is a pull-up bar. Wobbling and plopping down are the curriculum.
Commonly seen: night waking to practice standing (sometimes stuck standing and yelling), separation feelings at bedtime. It's development, not broken sleep habits.
Mattress to the lowest setting NOW if not already — pull-up plus old mattress height equals an escape attempt.

todo: Lower the crib mattress today
Practice controlled sit-downs: guide hips down so baby learns the exit move
Keep bedtime routine identical through the wobble — boring consistency wins
weeks.watching: Standing stuck and crying at 2 AM: calmly lay back down once, minimal fuss, repeat — it passes with practice.

weeks.summary: Side-stepping along furniture — cruising — commonly begins: the bridge between standing and walking.

happening.b: Baby maps the room by handholds: couch to table to chair. Expect falls onto the bottom — that's what diapers pad.
Bare feet grip and send the brain balance data; shoes are for outside protection later, not for learning to walk.
Head-height coffee-table corners become relevant — pad or retire the sharp ones this week.

todo: Arrange a safe cruising circuit with stable furniture
Corner-guards on sharp low tables
Skip walkers entirely — they're linked to injuries and don't speed walking
weeks.watching: After any fall: crying then normal behavior is reassuring; vomiting, unusual sleepiness or odd behavior after a head bump — call now.

weeks.summary: Thumb-and-finger pickup commonly clicks in around now — the grasp that separates humans from everything else, deployed on every crumb in your home.

happening.b: From raking whole-hand grabs to delicate thumb-finger precision: watch {name} pick up a single puff like a jeweler.
Pincer plus finger foods equals real self-feeding — slower and messier than spoon-feeding, and exactly the point.
The same precision finds every coin and button — the toilet-roll-tube test becomes a daily sweep.

todo: Offer pea-sized soft foods for pincer practice at meals
Daily floor sweep at crawl height
Let the mess happen — a tarp under the high chair, dignity preserved
weeks.watching: Blood-red streaks in stool after new foods, hives, or facial swelling — same-day pediatrician call.

weeks.summary: Communication goes gestural: pointing, arm-raising to be picked up, maybe a wave — and babble that sounds suspiciously deliberate.

happening.b: Pointing to show you things is a massive social-cognition step — {name} is deliberately steering YOUR attention. Answer every point like a question.
Waving, arms-up, head-shaking — gestures commonly arrive before first words and predict them. A rich gesture month is a great sign.
Syllable strings commonly land on mamamama/dadada — nonspecific at first, then aimed. The aimed version tends to arrive around the first-birthday season.

todo: Follow every point with naming: 'Dog! That's a dog'
Add gesture games: bye-bye, so-big, clapping
Read pointing books — 'where's the ball?' and wait
weeks.watching: No gestures at all (no pointing, waving, reaching to be picked up) by around 12 months — that's a specific thing to raise with your pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Vertical ambition arrives: stairs, couch cushions, the dishwasher door — everything is Everest, and a growth-hungry stretch commonly rides along.

happening.b: Crawling UP stairs commonly starts before any safe way down exists — gates top and bottom stop being optional.
A pre-10-month hungrier stretch is commonly seen: more solids interest, bigger portions, sometimes a extra milk feed.
Buttons that beep, lids that flip, balls that roll down ramps — baby is testing how the world responds.

todo: Install stair gates top AND bottom this week
Teach backwards-down-the-stairs as the house technique (later, supervised)
Anchor check: bookcases, dressers, TV — climbing changes the physics
weeks.watching: Loss of any acquired skill remains an always-call.

weeks.summary: A second wave of separation feelings commonly peaks near 10 months: daycare drop-offs and bedtime doors get dramatic again.

happening.b: Memory and attachment are stronger; object permanence now applies to YOU. Leaving hurts precisely because the bond built correctly.
Short, warm, predictable: same phrase, kiss, leave. Lingering and sneaking both commonly make it worse — the ritual is the reassurance.
A small lovey (for awake comfort; the crib stays bare for sleep under 12 months) commonly starts helping around now.

todo: Build a 10-second goodbye ritual and repeat it exactly
Leave baby with sitters awake, never mid-sleep
Play peek-a-boo and short hide-and-seek — separation practice disguised as fun
weeks.watching: Distress that never settles after you leave (not just at the door) — worth a conversation with your pediatrician or caregiver.

weeks.summary: Imitation becomes the main learning engine: {name} copies your phone-to-ear, your cup-sip, your fake cough — and studies your reactions like a scientist.

happening.b: Copying actions with objects (stirring, brushing, phoning) is commonly seen around now — it's how tool use and social behavior download.
Dropping food and watching your face, the fake cough for attention — {name} is mapping what moves you. Boring responses to unwanted behavior work better than lectures.
Holding a toy phone to the ear or 'drinking' from an empty cup — the first sparks of pretend play.

todo: Play copy-me games: clap, pat head, wave
Give real-life props: cup, spoon, brush, toy phone
Respond big to sounds-like-words — reinforcement grows them
weeks.watching: Molar-teething season may add drooly cranky days — same rules: no gels, no necklaces, cold teethers and patience.

weeks.summary: Letting go: brief hands-free standing commonly appears — two seconds of wobble that feel like a moon landing.

happening.b: Baby lets go of the couch, stands swaying, plops down, repeats. Each rep calibrates the balance system — falls onto the bottom are part of the spec.
Picking a toy off the floor from standing and returning up — a deceptively big strength milestone commonly practiced endlessly.
A stable push-walker (NOT a seated walker) gives supported walking practice on baby's own power.

todo: Cheer the attempts, ignore the falls — your calm is the safety signal
Offer a heavy stable push toy on carpet first
Keep floors clear of rolling hazards along cruise routes
weeks.watching: Persistent toe-walking only, or legs that seem asymmetric in strength — mention at the 12-month visit.

weeks.summary: First true words commonly appear anywhere from now through 14+ months: 'mama' aimed at mama, 'ba' meaning ball — meaning attached to sound.

happening.b: Any consistent sound aimed at a consistent thing counts — 'baba' for bottle is a word even if the phonetics need years of polish.
Receptive language leads: {name} likely understands 'no', own name, 'where's daddy?' and simple requests long before saying much.
Point-and-name everything, then pause. The pause is where speech grows — leave silences for {name} to fill.

todo: Keep a first-words list in notes — it becomes a treasure
Ask simple 'where is…?' questions and celebrate the looks/points
Sing the same few songs on repeat — repetition builds prediction builds words
weeks.watching: No response to quiet sounds or name across days — hearing check conversation with the pediatrician.

weeks.summary: Cooperation debut: arms into sleeves, holding still-ish for diapers, handing you objects on request — {name} joins the team.

happening.b: 'Give me the ball', 'come here' with a gesture — commonly understood around now. Each followed request is language plus social wiring.
Baby gives you things to see your reaction, then wants them back — an exchange loop that's pure social practice.
Predictable sequences (bath→book→bed) commonly reduce protest — the routine IS the explanation for a pre-verbal person.

todo: Narrate routines with the same words daily
Ask for the object back with an open hand and 'thank you!'
Let baby 'help': hold the spoon, pat the laundry — slow, worth it
weeks.watching: Nothing urgent this week — enjoy the cooperation window before toddler opinions arrive.

weeks.summary: The pre-birthday sprint: cruising fast, maybe steps behind a push toy, opinions forming and loudly filed.

happening.b: Protesting a taken toy, arching at the car seat, insisting on self-feeding — will and preference are developmental progress wearing an inconvenient costume.
Three meals plus two-ish snacks commonly becomes the shape; milk feeds consolidate. Appetite varies day to day — the week's average is the honest measure.
Short board books at the same daily slots build the reading reflex — {name} may already turn pages and point at favorites.

todo: Offer two acceptable choices where possible — 'red cup or blue?'
Keep car-seat rules non-negotiable but boring — no drama fuel
Photograph the almost-walking wobble — it disappears fast
weeks.watching: Fewer wet diapers or dark urine as milk feeds shift — nudge water sips with meals and mention if persistent.

weeks.summary: One month to the birthday: 12-month checkup booking, the whole-milk transition ahead, and a party that should be smaller than the internet suggests.

happening.b: Growth, development review, and a vaccine round (commonly including MMR and others per schedule) — book it now if not on the calendar.
At 12 months, formula typically ends and whole cow's milk can begin (breastfeeding continues as long as you both want). No transition needed before the birthday — just a heads-up.
One-year-olds enjoy: one balloon, cake destruction, a nap on schedule. Keep it short, small and near naptime-free hours — the party is for the adults' memories, and that's fine.

todo: Book the 12-month checkup
Plan the party around sleep, not against it
Start offering an open cup with water at meals — skill for the milk switch
weeks.watching: Nothing new to watch — steady as she goes into the birthday month.

weeks.summary: The famous window is open: first independent steps commonly land anywhere from ~9 to 18 months — this stretch is prime time, and every baby picks their own day.

happening.b: One to three drunken-sailor steps between supports, then a proud collapse. Walking 'clicks' over days to weeks after that — regressions to crawling for speed are normal.

happening.t: Late walking is usually just late
happening.b: A confident cruiser who won't let go yet is commonly just cautious. The 18-month mark is when not-walking becomes a formal conversation — before that, temperament rules.
As legs take transport, hands free up — expect carrying objects everywhere and the first throw experiments.

todo: Set up a step-gap: two stable supports a step apart, toy on the far one
Stay one step away with open arms — the best walking lure ever built
Film everything this month
weeks.watching: Consistent inability to bear weight on legs at all — that's a pediatrician conversation now, not at 18 months.

weeks.summary: Reach and cleverness compound: babyproofing needs its level-two audit before walking multiplies the range.

happening.b: Standing reach + pincer grasp + imitation = drawers opened, buttons pushed, plants taxed. Audit at standing height this time.
Cabinet locks where chemicals/meds live, stove-knob covers, toilet lock if lid-fascination appears, cords for blinds shortened, door pinch-guards on favorites.
All medicines — including vitamins and grandma's purse stash — up high AND locked. Purses at floor level are the classic miss.

todo: Do the standing-height audit room by room
Lock the under-sink kingdom
Brief every visiting adult: bags up high
weeks.watching: Poison Control number saved in your phone: 1-800-222-1222 — hopefully never needed, cheap to have.

weeks.summary: One week to the birthday: a good moment to look at how far you've BOTH come — the person who opened this app at week 1 wouldn't believe the current you.

happening.b: Twelve months ago: reflexes and 18-hour sleep. Now: opinions, jokes, gestures, maybe steps and words. That arc happened in your living room.
Open the sleep stats and scroll back — the night that felt endless in week 6 is a dot on a curve that bent your way. You logged the proof.
Nobody tracks it, so we will: you learned a language with no dictionary, ran a year of night shifts and kept a human alive and thriving. Worth logging.

todo: Scroll your own history in the app — seriously, do it
Write {name} a two-line birthday note; future-you will cry appropriately
Take the one-year photo in the same spot as the newborn one if you have it
weeks.watching: Nothing to watch. Take the lap.

weeks.summary: Week 52: cake, the 12-month checkup with its vaccine round, and the official milk transition — a big week for a small person.

happening.b: Commonly by now: pulling to stand or steps, a word or two with meaning, pointing and waving, finding hidden objects, feeding self finger foods.
The 12-month set (commonly MMR among others) can bring a delayed mild reaction — a fever or faint rash 7–12 days later is a known pattern; your pediatrician will brief you.
Formula retires; whole cow's milk enters (about 16–24 oz/day, in cups more than bottles) alongside real food. Breastfeeding continues as long as you both like.

todo: Do vaccines a day or two away from the party if you can
Start milk as an open-cup drink with meals
Begin the slow bottle phase-out — cups take over from here
weeks.watching: After 12-month shots: fever spikes above 104°F, or any reaction that worries you — call; the delayed-fever pattern is worth knowing in advance.

weeks.summary: Welcome to toddlerhood: whether walking or про-cruising, {name} is officially a toddler — with the appetite shift to prove it.

happening.b: After the first year's tripling act, growth rate drops — and appetite commonly drops with it. A toddler eating 'nothing' for a day and feasting the next is running standard firmware.
Your job: offer variety on schedule. Their job: decide what and how much. This division of labor, held calmly, prevents most feeding battles before they start.
Expect wide-stance, arms-up 'high guard' walking, faceplants onto carpet, and mileage that doubles daily.

todo: Serve tiny portions — seconds available on request
Keep milk to meals/snacks so it doesn't replace food
Retire the infant bathtub if standing up mid-bath became a sport — non-slip mat era
weeks.watching: A truly shrinking child (weight curve dropping across visits) is a doctor conversation; a picky Tuesday is not.

weeks.summary: The vocabulary trickle: a few real words plus a rich gesture-and-grunt system that communicates shockingly well.

happening.b: A handful of words at this age is commonly seen; understanding ('bring the shoe', 'where's the cat?') runs far ahead and matters more.
Long babble monologues with adult intonation and zero real words — sounds like a phone call in another language, and it's healthy speech practice.
Pointing now MEANS 'I want that' — respond with the name before the object: 'Banana? Here's the banana.'

todo: Name the pointed thing every time before handing it over
Read the same favorite books on loop — repetition is the engine
Trade screen background noise for household narration where you can
weeks.watching: No words AND no gestures by now — bring it up with the pediatrician rather than waiting for 18 months.

weeks.summary: Walking (or nearly): distance and confidence compound daily, and the world reorganizes around a mobile toddler.

happening.b: Wide stance and high arms first; smoother stride, stopping without sitting, and carrying-while-walking come over the next months. Falls remain constant; concern doesn't.
Grass, sand, slight slopes — uneven terrain is balance training no toy can match. First real shoes: flexible, roomy, only for outside.
Chairs, couches, stairs, you — everything is a route. Spotting beats forbidding: teach feet-first-down as the house rule.

todo: Daily outdoor walking time, terrain varied
Buy shoes measured, flexible, and slightly roomy
Practice backwards-down on stairs together, every time
weeks.watching: Falls with head bumps: crying-then-normal reassures; vomiting, sleepiness, or acting off afterwards — call now.

weeks.summary: Trial and error rules: dumping, stacking, banging, dropping from the high chair — each rep is physics research with a lab assistant (you).

happening.b: Two-block towers, containers emptied and refilled — commonly the core play. The knock-down is not sabotage; it's the second half of the experiment.
Spoon attempts (mostly inverted), pushing buttons that beep, pulling the string to get the toy — means-to-end thinking coming online.
Doing the forbidden thing WHILE watching you — boundary research, not defiance. A calm, boring, consistent 'no + redirect' is the effective data you can provide.

todo: Give stacking cups and a dump-truck-grade container
Let the spoon chaos happen — self-feeding accuracy comes from misses
Pick your few real no's and hold them identically every time
weeks.watching: Nothing urgent — molars may cameo with drooly nights; cold teethers still the answer.

weeks.summary: A growth-and-skills push toward 15 months: bigger appetite days, new words trickling, and the 15-month checkup on the horizon.

happening.b: Commonly 3–10ish words by 15 months with huge normal variance — plus 'jargoning' monologues and reliable gesture communication.
'Get the ball and bring it here' starts landing — memory holding two steps is new machinery.
The 15-month visit: growth, milestones, commonly another vaccine installment per schedule. Book it now.

todo: Book the 15-month visit
Play fetch-style two-step games
Keep the first-words list growing — screenshot it for the visit
weeks.watching: Loss of any words or skills previously had — always the same rule: call, don't wait.

weeks.summary: First molars commonly arrive in this stretch — bigger teeth, grumpier nights, familiar playbook.

happening.b: More surface breaking through means several drooly, cheek-rubbing, night-waking days per tooth — commonly seen and finite.
Cold teethers, chilled washcloth, extra patience. Still no numbing gels, still no amber necklaces — the guidance hasn't changed, the tooth just got bigger.
Teething may nudge temperature slightly; real fever means something else. The thermometer settles the debate that cheeks start.

todo: Stock the freezer-adjacent teether rotation
Brush the newcomers: soft brush, rice-grain smear of fluoride toothpaste, twice daily
Protect the bedtime routine through the grumpy nights
weeks.watching: Fever 100.4°F+, ear pulling with distress, or feeding refusal — that's illness protocol, not teething.

weeks.summary: 'Self! Me do it!' — before those words exist, the behavior arrives: self-feeding insistence, wriggling out of help, strong preferences.

happening.b: Insisting on the spoon, refusing the coat, choosing the other cup — toddler independence is developmental homework, delivered loudly.
Two acceptable options beat open questions and beat commands: 'stairs or elevator?' works when 'come here' starts a negotiation.
Transitions (leaving the park, starting the bath) go smoother with rituals and warnings: 'one more slide, then shoes' — then actually one more slide.

todo: Offer controlled choices at friction points
Build a leaving-the-fun ritual and honor it exactly
Budget double time for anything involving toddler 'help'
weeks.watching: Nothing clinical — just save your no's for safety and let the coat stay unzipped sometimes.

weeks.summary: A patterns week: your logs now hold a story — sleep consolidation, feeding evolution, growth curve — worth a five-minute review.

happening.b: Commonly: one solid night block with occasional molar/leap interruptions and two naps, with the 2→1 nap transition looming somewhere in the next months.
Three meals, snacks, milk in cups — the graph from cluster-feeding chaos to this is one of parenting's quiet victories.
When the morning nap starts sabotaging the afternoon one or bedtime, the one-nap era begins — commonly 14–18 months, arriving gradually.

todo: Scroll your stats month-view — pattern-spotting is free reassurance
If naps start fighting each other, nudge the morning nap later by 15-minute steps
Update the growth chart at every measure
weeks.watching: A toddler who stops climbing/walking as before, limps, or regresses in energy across days — pediatrician call.

weeks.summary: Receptive language explodes: {name} understands far more than the word count shows — including, inconveniently, words you spell out.

happening.b: Understanding runs months ahead of speaking. Following requests, pointing to body parts, reacting to plans overheard — the inbox is much bigger than the outbox.
'Where's your nose?' commonly becomes a hit around now — naming games wire vocabulary faster than flashcards ever will.
'More milk', 'daddy go' — combinations may appear for some toddlers now, for many closer to 18–24 months. Both timelines are standard issue.

todo: Play the body-part naming game at diaper changes
Expand toddler words: they say 'ball' — you say 'yes, the red ball rolls!'
Keep narration going; it's compounding interest now
weeks.watching: By 15 months: no words at all, no pointing, or not following simple requests — raise it at the visit rather than waiting.

weeks.summary: Movement diversifies: walking backward, almost-running, stooping, climbing onto everything — the motor résumé fills fast.

happening.b: Walking while pulling a toy, backing up, squatting to inspect, first stiff-legged running attempts — commonly appearing through this stretch.
Deliberate throwing (of balls, ideally) starts — a skill AND a dinner-table hazard. Redirect the arm, don't cancel the program.
Low slides with help, swings, ramps — playgrounds become genuine gross-motor gyms at this age.

todo: Daily gross-motor outlet — weather-proof a backup indoor option
Trade 'don't throw' for 'throw the BALL' + a target
Teach climbing DOWN from the couch feet-first as a skill, not a scold
weeks.watching: Persistent tip-toe-only walking or one-sided movement patterns — mention at the 15-month visit.

weeks.summary: Proto-tantrums debut: big feelings, small vocabulary, zero patience — the combination is loud and completely on schedule.

happening.b: Wants are specific, words are few, impulse control is years away. Frustration overflow is a hardware limitation, not a discipline failure.
Your regulation is the borrowed regulation: low voice, simple words, staying near. Reasoning mid-meltdown doesn't land; presence does.
Hunger, tiredness and transitions cause most eruptions — snacks, protected naps and warning rituals prevent more tantrums than any technique resolves.

todo: Name feelings simply: 'You're mad. The block fell.'
Keep a snack in every bag forever
Pick battles: safety yes, mismatched socks no
weeks.watching: Breath-holding spells during hard crying (brief, scary-looking, commonly harmless) — worth describing to your pediatrician once to confirm the pattern.

weeks.summary: The 15-month checkup closes this guide's arc: from reflexes to a walking, gesturing, opinionated small person — and your library here stays with you.

happening.b: Commonly: walking (or nearly), several words plus rich gestures, following simple directions, imitating chores, stacking, self-feeding chunks.
Growth, development screen, commonly a vaccine installment; bring the first-words list, sleep questions and any Worth-watching leftovers.
The tracker, stats, Ask and your history keep working past the guide — the weekly chapters end here, the companion doesn't.

todo: Bring logs, words list and doctor-notes to the 15-month visit
Ask about the 2→1 nap timing for YOUR kid's pattern
Celebrate: 64 weeks of showing up, logged and lived
weeks.watching: The standing rules survive the guide: fever thresholds, skill regressions and your gut feeling always warrant the call.
